newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates end see-saw to end up.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates end see-saw to end up.

text.p: Pakistan's money rates fluctuated before ending up on Monday as the market was unsure about the liquidity status of the market, but dealers said rates might open up on Tuesday as the market closed short.

Overnight rates hovered at 19 to 19.5 percent in early trade but most closing deals were seen at 20 percent, one dealer said. Offers for one-week funds were at 20 percent, but borrowers showed no interest amid uncertainty about market liquidity.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan received bids worth a total of 10.247 billion rupees in an auction of six-month federal bonds with yields from 16.70 to 17.49 percent, he said.
The result of the auction was expected to be announced later on Monday.
